title: Convert DR exercise evidence into maintained readiness: decision comparison 1
teachingQuestion: How does an exercise observation become a verified, owned, and retested recovery improvement?
focalInsight: Observation, evidence, finding, owner/action, plan change, retest, and truthful test status.
caption: Compare meaning, decision conditions, and failures. These concise distinctions are paired with the worked examples in the teaching unit.

nodes.label: Test Evidence
nodes.definition: Time-stamped artifacts that substantiate what was attempted, observed, decided, and achieved in a test.
nodes.decision: Collect evidence tied to the objective and protect its integrity before interpreting a pass/fail result.
nodes.failureExample: A verbal claim that “failover worked” cannot establish recovery time, data state, or authorization.
nodes.detail: Time-stamped artifacts that substantiate what was attempted, observed, decided, and achieved in a test.

nodes.label: Exercise Observation
nodes.definition: A recorder’s factual note about behavior, timing, deviation, or condition during an exercise.
nodes.decision: Record facts and context first; do not label it a failure until the expected condition and evidence are compared.
nodes.failureExample: Treating an uncorroborated impression as a finding can send remediation at the wrong problem.
nodes.detail: A recorder’s factual note about behavior, timing, deviation, or condition during an exercise.

nodes.label: DR Finding
nodes.definition: A validated gap between an expected recovery condition and observed evidence, with stated impact and confidence.
nodes.decision: Classify it by capability, documentation, process, or ownership and link it to the challenged recovery assumption.
nodes.failureExample: A finding with no stated consequence cannot be prioritized or accepted as risk.
nodes.detail: A validated gap between an expected recovery condition and observed evidence, with stated impact and confidence.

nodes.label: Corrective Action
nodes.definition: A specific change assigned to an accountable owner to address a validated finding, with due date and acceptance evidence.
nodes.decision: Assign action only after the finding is understood; record dependencies and an explicit risk disposition if it cannot be completed.
nodes.failureExample: “Update DR plan” without owner or acceptance test creates an untrackable promise.
nodes.detail: A specific change assigned to an accountable owner to address a validated finding, with due date and acceptance evidence.

nodes.label: Lessons Learned
nodes.definition: A reusable conclusion that explains why the observed result occurred and changes future recovery decisions or capability.
nodes.decision: Derive lessons from supported findings across the exercise; avoid turning blame or a single anecdote into a general rule.
nodes.failureExample: A blame-focused lesson discourages reporting and leaves the system condition unchanged.
nodes.detail: A reusable conclusion that explains why the observed result occurred and changes future recovery decisions or capability.

nodes.label: Plan Maintenance
nodes.definition: Controlled updating of contacts, assumptions, diagrams, procedures, and commitments as conditions change.
nodes.decision: Update the plan through change control after a verified need; identify which plan element and dependency changed.
nodes.failureExample: A stale contact list can make an otherwise sound recovery design unusable during activation.
nodes.detail: Controlled updating of contacts, assumptions, diagrams, procedures, and commitments as conditions change.

nodes.label: Retest
nodes.definition: A proportionate repeat exercise that demonstrates the specific corrected condition now works.
nodes.decision: Retest the failed path and predefined acceptance evidence, not merely a different easy scenario.
nodes.failureExample: Closing a ticket after editing a document without exercising the changed handoff leaves the capability unverified.
nodes.detail: A proportionate repeat exercise that demonstrates the specific corrected condition now works.

nodes.label: Test Status
nodes.definition: An accurate statement of what scope/objectives passed, failed, were untested, or remain at risk.
nodes.decision: Communicate status with scope and limitations to the appropriate decision makers; never equate schedule completion with readiness.
nodes.failureExample: A blanket “passed” report can cause leaders to accept recovery risk they were never shown.
nodes.detail: An accurate statement of what scope/objectives passed, failed, were untested, or remain at risk.

nodes.label: Regulator Communication
nodes.definition: A governed disclosure to a regulator about exercise status or material gaps when a legal, contractual, or supervisory obligation applies.
nodes.decision: Use counsel/compliance-approved triggers, audience, timing, and facts; do not invent a reporting duty from the exercise alone.
nodes.failureExample: An unapproved disclosure can be inaccurate or omit required facts; silence can breach an applicable duty.
nodes.detail: A governed disclosure to a regulator about exercise status or material gaps when a legal, contractual, or supervisory obligation applies.

learningContract.teachingQuestion: How does an exercise observation become a verified, owned, and retested recovery improvement?
learningContract.misconception: Finishing on time, updating a plan, or logging an issue proves recovery readiness.
learningContract.formRationale: Aligned columns make concept meanings, decision criteria and failure consequences explicit and comparable.
learningContract.focalInsight: Observation, evidence, finding, owner/action, plan change, retest, and truthful test status.
learningContract.intentionalOmissions: Do not prescribe a universal severity scale, retention duration, or external reporting rule.
learningContract.retrievalPrompt: An observer says “the team seemed confused”; what evidence is needed before creating a DR finding, and what closes it?
